change: Resolve the living sword owner immediately before each strike; a sword whose owner was killed earlier in the same tick no longer crashes the arena or strikes after death. Remove dead and expired swords after processing.

assessment.scope: Server and WebSocket clients only; no browser rendering or long-duration guarantee.

storageDedup.policy: All historical paths and bytes preserved. Treat linked snapshots as immutable; future replacement must be atomic, never in-place.

limitations: The 70-player test is a short synthetic run on a shared VPS with 3 CPU including load drivers, not maximum CCU or browser FPS
Other 70-player runs fell below 19 Hz; no admission limit was raised and the capacity issue remains open
The 16 MiB checkpoint threshold remains a separate uninstalled candidate; its run crashed on the pre-existing sword bug and has no qualified performance result
Memory of the complete world, PostgreSQL prepare work and independent room ownership remain open
All backup paths and bytes are retained; deduplicated historical snapshots must never be edited in place
Cold startup took approximately 117 seconds; no restart loop, but startup latency remains open
validationNotes:
Initial new test fixture had a missing brace; corrected, first output preserved.
Differential malformed-input fixture compared an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate with encoded UTF-8; expected value now reads the same bytes as production.
A relative restore path used the wrong cwd; no files changed; corrected from workspace root, reran 32 tests on final v2.
One SSH upload failed before handshake; retry completed before remote staging.
Buffered v2 selected. Byte-search v3 and regex v4 were slower on Linux and were excluded. All outputs/source files remain in artifacts.
The SSH downloader rejected the tmpfs archive path before reading. A checksum-verified durable copy was created inside the allowed test stand, then downloaded and verified locally.
The first 40-second readiness probe expired during cold startup. The process remained active with NRestarts=0 and entry closed; readiness was awaited without restarting it.
A second readiness window expired; the third passed. The same process began listening approximately 88 seconds after start and PostgreSQL reached the expected revision. No restart was triggered.
The first generated capacity guard failed local syntax validation because a replacement string interpreted dollar-apostrophe. Replaced through a callback, saved the rejected file, and reran syntax validation before upload; no remote run used it.
The 70-player native baseline finished simulation and PG comparison, but its harness exited PG_OPERATION_FAILED before final ACK/schema-cleanup evidence. Original summary and logs retained. An independent audit recovered all 2080 ACKs, and the exact random test schema was then removed. The first exit remains a recorded failure; its exact transient cause is not proven.
70-threshold aborted with TypeError in positionSword: another sword killed its owner during updateSwords. The original failed summary and stdout/stderr remain unchanged. Independent abnormal-exit audit recovered all 775 ACKs, no duplicates; PostgreSQL revision1524 lagged WAL2246 at crash. The isolated PG snapshot was exported before dropping only its random synthetic schema. Threshold performance is unqualified, candidate not installed.
New real-physics regression test reproduced the same null.targetX error before the fix (sword-regression-before.txt). After per-sword liveness validation and final cleanup, Windows87 passed. New source92cc7c4 touches one runtime file plus its test.
First full-source verification helper lacked the prior manifest locally and failed ENOENT without mutating any source. Fetched the existing remote manifest, then all3231 files matched the new candidate exactly; only the expected two paths differ from prior full suite.
Disk: SHA and exact mode/uid/gid/mtime verified for45 immutable historical recovery-file paths;42 replaced atomically with hardlinks to3 identical canonical files. All paths/bytes retained,1204128814 bytes reclaimed; independent local files verified first. Never overwrite these linked backup files in place.
One SSH metadata download lost connection before handshake during sword release backup transfer; retried successfully. Backup bytes were independently downloaded and checked against their SHA and full world/PG contents.
Sword release cold startup exceeded the readiness polling window; the next readiness check succeeded with the same PID479513 and NRestarts0. Entry remained closed throughout. Readiness was reported at syncedAt1795464129391, roughly117 seconds after systemd start; cold startup remains an open performance issue.
First post-start calendar comparison rejected one profile notice/revision and world revision: an old clan-chest expiry notification reached its exact24h deadline1795464108779 during cold startup after restartAt1795464012061. Original verifier is saved as sword-stability-install-20261124/verify-calendar-first.cjs; first failure retained in tool log. Existing clan-chest-rewards.expire removes only notifications at n.at+DAY, not chest rewards. Verifier now derives the exact deadline from each removed old notice and replays it after constructor/startup, still requiring complete equality of every world/auxiliary field. Game runtime and game data were not modified to force a match. Entry stays closed until the stronger replay and full PG read succeed.
Second calendar verifier attempt also rejected: an already-expired notice deadline was inserted before the evidenced constructor time, causing a newly-created expiry notification to receive the wrong replay timestamp. Saved verify-calendar-notice-first.cjs. Corrected verifier adds only deadlines later than the first evidenced calendar transition, preserving actual constructor time and exact timestamp equality. No live code or data changes.

limitations: One short live CPU sample, after the five-minute observation, not matched A/B or maximum capacity
CPU percentages include idle time; inclusive entries overlap and cannot be added
RSS is process-wide and must not be summed across workers

findings.next: Addressable profiles and separated history are still required to avoid re-reading and hashing the entire world; main-thread physics and worker transfers need a reproducible large-part benchmark
